html:
The Kizh are an Indigenous people of the Los Angeles Basin, a group of descendants of the Mission Indians of San Gabriel, often called Gabrieleño. The name Kizh comes from an early name for the Gabrieleño speaking people.

Before the Spanish, these peoples lived in many villages from the San Gabriel Mountains to the coast and the Channel Islands, fishing, gathering acorns and trading with the Chumash. In 1771 the Spanish founded Mission San Gabriel, one of the California missions, and brought most of them into it. Today descendants differ over what to call themselves: Kizh or Tongva. Their neighbours included the Tataviam to the north and the Acjachemen to the south.
